63899-the-giants-return.title: The Giants Return
63899-the-giants-return.creator: Unknown
63899-the-giants-return.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. captain, came slowly down the narrow stair from the observatory, into the big rotunda that was now the main recreation room, where most of the people gathered. The great chamber, a full cross-section of the vessel, had been at first a fuel hold.

arxiv-1401-3222.title: Uncovering nodes that spread information between communities in social networks
arxiv-1401-3222.creator: AVMAlexander V. Mantzaris
arxiv-1401-3222.description: A 2014 arXiv research paper by AVMAlexander V. Mantzaris. From many datasets gathered in online social networks, well defined community structures have been observed. A large number of users participate in these networks and the size of the resulting graphs poses computational challenges.

arxiv-1807-07091.title: Language Preservation Problems in Parametric Timed Automata
arxiv-1807-07091.creator: Étienne André, Didier Lime, Nicolas Markey
arxiv-1807-07091.description: Abstract . Parametric timed automata (PTA) are a powerful formalism to model and reason about concurrent systems with some unknown timing delays. In this paper, we address the (untimed) language- and trace-preservation problems: given a reference parameter valuation, does there exist another parameter valuation with the same untimed language, or with the same set of traces?

arxiv-2012-10711.title: Quantum reinforcement learning in continuous action space
arxiv-2012-10711.creator: Shaojun Wu, Shan Jin, Dingding Wen, Donghong Han, Xiaoting Wang †
arxiv-2012-10711.description: Abstract Quantum reinforcement learning (QRL) is a promising paradigm for near-term quantum devices. While existing QRL methods have shown success in discrete action spaces, extending these techniques to continuous domains is challenging due to the curse of dimensionality introduced by discretization.

arxiv-2202-03699.title: Assessing Planetary Complexity and Potential Agnostic Biosignatures using Epsilon Machines
arxiv-2202-03699.creator: Stuart Bartlett, Jiazheng Li, Lixiang Gu, Lana Sinapayen, Siteng Fan, Vijay Natraj, Jonathan Jiang, David Crisp, Yuk Yung
arxiv-2202-03699.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Stuart Bartlett, Jiazheng Li, Lixiang Gu, Lana Sinapayen, Siteng Fan, Vijay Natraj, Jonathan Jiang, David Crisp, Yuk Yung. We present a new approach to exoplanet characterisation using techniques from complexity science, with potential applications to biosignature detection. This agnostic method makes use of the temporal variability of light reflected or emitted from a planet. We use a technique known as epsilon machine reconstruction to compute the statistical complexity, a measure of the minimal model size for time series data.

arxiv-2206-02700.title: Forbidding Edges between Points in the Plane to Disconnect the Triangulation Flip Graph
arxiv-2206-02700.creator: Reza Bigdeli, Anna Lubiw
arxiv-2206-02700.description: Abstract The flip graph for a set P P of points in the plane has a vertex for every triangulation of P P , and an edge when two triangulations differ by one flip that replaces one triangulation edge by another.

arxiv-2210-04549.title: A pasting theorem for iterated Segal spaces
arxiv-2210-04549.creator: Jaco Ruit
arxiv-2210-04549.description: Abstract . We introduce a novel notion of pasting shapes for iterated Segal spaces which classify particular arrangements of composing cells in d d -uple Segal spaces. Using this formalism, we then continue to prove a pasting theorem for these iterated Segal spaces. 1.

arxiv-2212-05089.title: FMO Study of the Interaction Energy between Human Estrogen Receptor α \alpha and Selected Ligands
arxiv-2212-05089.creator: Ricardo Ugarte
arxiv-2212-05089.description: Abstract Fragment molecular orbital (FMO) calculations were performed in aqueous media which allowed us to obtain the interaction energy between the human estrogen receptor α \alpha ligand-binding domain (ER) and the selected ligands (L): 17 β \beta -estradiol (E2), 17 α \alpha -estradiol (17 α \alpha -E2), estriol (E3), genistein (GNT), diethylstilbestrol (DES), bisphenol A (BPA), bisphenol AF (BPAF), hydroxychlor

arxiv-2301-04018.title: Origin of heterogeneous stripping of lithium in liquid electrolytes
arxiv-2301-04018.creator: Martin Werres, Yaobin Xu, Hao Jia, Chongmin Wang, Wu Xu, Arnulf Latz, Birger Horstmann
arxiv-2301-04018.description: Abstract Lithium metal batteries suffer from low cycle life. During discharge, parts of the lithium are not stripped reversibly and remain isolated from the current collector. This isolated lithium is trapped in the insulating remaining solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) shell and contributes to the capacity loss.

arxiv-2406-12909.title: Scalable Training of Trustworthy and Energy-Efficient Predictive Graph Foundation Models for Atomistic Materials Modeling: A Case Study with HydraGNN
arxiv-2406-12909.creator: Massimiliano Lupo Pasini, Jong Youl Choi, Kshitij Mehta, Pei Zhang, David Rogers, Jonghyun Bae, Khaled Z. Ibrahim, Ashwin M. Aji, Karl W. Schulz, Jordà Polo, Prasanna Balaprakash
arxiv-2406-12909.description: Abstract We present our work on developing and training scalable, trustworthy, and energy-efficient predictive graph foundation models (GFMs) using HydraGNN, a multi-headed graph convolutional neural network architecture. HydraGNN expands the boundaries of graph neural network (GNN) computations in both training scale and data diversity.

arxiv-2407-04385.title: Impact of LRG1 and LRG2 in DESI 2024 BAO data on dark energy evolution
arxiv-2407-04385.creator: Guanlin Liu, Yu Wang, Wen Zhao
arxiv-2407-04385.description: Abstract Recent measurements of baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) suggest a preference for a dynamic dark energy model over a cosmological constant. This conclusion emerges from the combination of DESI’s BAO data with observations of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) and various type Ia supernova (SN Ia) catalogues.

arxiv-2409-18265.title: Task-recency bias strikes back: Adapting covariances in Exemplar-Free Class Incremental Learning
arxiv-2409-18265.creator: Grzegorz Rypeść, Sebastian Cygert, Tomasz Trzciński, Bartłomiej Twardowski
arxiv-2409-18265.description: Abstract Exemplar-Free Class Incremental Learning (EFCIL) tackles the problem of training a model on a sequence of tasks without access to past data. Existing state-of-the-art methods represent classes as Gaussian distributions in the feature extractor’s latent space, enabling Bayes classification or training the classifier by replaying pseudo features.

arxiv-2410-01917.title: Provably Accurate Shapley Value Estimation via Leverage Score Sampling
arxiv-2410-01917.creator: Christopher Musco, R. Teal Witter
arxiv-2410-01917.description: Abstract Originally introduced in game theory, Shapley values have emerged as a central tool in explainable machine learning, where they are used to attribute model predictions to specific input features. However, computing Shapley values exactly is expensive: for a general model with n n features, O ⁡ ( 2 n ) O(2^{n}) model evaluations are necessary.

arxiv-2411-03851.title: On a probabilistic global optimizer derived from the Walker slice sampling
arxiv-2411-03851.creator: Aditya Gupta, Souvik Das, Debasish Chatterjee
arxiv-2411-03851.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Aditya Gupta, Souvik Das, Debasish Chatterjee. This article presents a zeroth order probabilistic global optimization algorithm — 𝖲𝗐𝗂𝖿𝗍𝖭𝖺𝗏 \mathsf{SwiftNav} — for (not necessarily convex) functions over a compact domain. A discretization procedure is deployed on the compact domain, starting with a small step-size h > 0 h>0 and subsequently adaptively refining it in the course of a simulated annealing routine utilizing the Walker slice and the Gibbs sampler, in order to identify a set of global optimizers up to good precision.

arxiv-2501-00034.title: Time Series Feature Redundancy Paradox: An Empirical Study Based on Mortgage Default Prediction
arxiv-2501-00034.creator: Chengyue Huang *, Yahe Yang
arxiv-2501-00034.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chengyue Huang *, Yahe Yang. With the widespread application of machine learning in financial risk management, conventional wisdom suggests that longer training periods and more feature variables contribute to improved model performance. This paper, focusing on mortgage default prediction, empirically discovers a phenomenon that contradicts traditional knowledge: in time series prediction, increased training data timespan and additional non-critical features actually lead to significant deterioration in prediction effectiveness.

arxiv-2503-22388.title: Why Stop at One Error? Benchmarking LLMs as Data Science Code Debuggers for Multi-Hop and Multi-Bug Errors
arxiv-2503-22388.creator: Zhiyu Yang, Shuo Wang, Yukun Yan, Yang Deng
arxiv-2503-22388.description: Abstract LLMs are transforming software development, yet most code benchmarks still emphasize syntactic or functional correctness in simple, single-error cases. These settings miss the core difficulty of real-world data science debugging, where runtime errors propagate across multiple lines (multi-hop) and often appear in sets (multi-bug).

arxiv-2505-00553.title: The Jackknife method as a new approach to validate strong lens mass models
arxiv-2505-00553.creator: Shun Nishida 1, Masamune Oguri 1,2, Yoshinobu Fudamoto 2,3, Ayari Kitamura 4
arxiv-2505-00553.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Shun Nishida 1, Masamune Oguri 1,2, Yoshinobu Fudamoto 2,3, Ayari Kitamura 4. The accuracy of a mass model in the strong lensing analysis is crucial for unbiased predictions of physical quantities such as magnifications and time delays.

arxiv-2505-11487.title: Area and volume from entangled qubits
arxiv-2505-11487.creator: Juan M. Romero, Emiliano Montoya-González
arxiv-2505-11487.description: Abstract In this paper a relation between entangled states and geometry is studied. In particular, the area of 2 ​ D 2D parallelogram is obtained from an entangled 4 4 -qubit state. In addition, the vector area of a 3 ​ D 3D parallelogram is derived from entangled 6 6 -qubit states.

arxiv-2509-17993.title: StableGuard: Towards Unified Copyright Protection and Tamper Localization in Latent Diffusion Models
arxiv-2509-17993.creator: Haoxin Yang, Bangzhen Liu, Xuemiao Xu, Cheng Xu, Yuyang Yu, Zikai Huang, Yi Wang, Shengfeng He, Homepage: https://github.com/Harxis/StableGuard
arxiv-2509-17993.description: Abstract The advancement of diffusion models has enhanced the realism of AI-generated content but also raised concerns about misuse, necessitating robust copyright protection and tampering localization. Although recent methods have made progress toward unified solutions, their reliance on post hoc processing introduces considerable application inconvenience and compromises forensic reliability.

europmc-pmc3488411.title: Challenges and opportunities for small molecule aptamer development.
europmc-pmc3488411.creator: McKeague M, Derosa MC.
europmc-pmc3488411.description: Aptamers are single-stranded oligonucleotides that bind to targets with high affinity and selectivity. Their use as molecular recognition elements has emerged as a viable approach for biosensing, diagnostics, and therapeutics. Despite this potential, relatively few aptamers...

pmc-10569605.title: Impact of COVID-19 on the treatment of depressive patients in Germany–a gap in care for the mentally ill?
pmc-10569605.creator: Mareike Aichholzer, Carmen Schiweck, Carmen Uckermark, Tirage Hamzehloiya, Christine Reif-Leonhard, Rejane Golbach, Andreas Reif, Sharmili Edwin Thanarajah
pmc-10569605.description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic led to a higher incidence of depression and a worsening of psychiatric conditions, while pre-existing constraints of the healthcare system and safety regulations limited psychiatric care.AimsWe investigated the impact of the pandemic on the clinical care of patients with a single episode (SE-MDD) or major depressive disorder (MDD) in Germany.

pmc-11308078.title: Proteomics Analysis Provides Insights into the Role of Lipid Metabolism in T2DM-Related Sarcopenia
pmc-11308078.creator: Jingying Wu, Shengnan Wang, Huafeng Zhuang, Weichun Wang, Yaoguo Wang, Youfang Chen, Zhengping Huang, Chunnuan Chen, Xiaofeng Chen
pmc-11308078.description: Sarcopenia has been recognized as an emerging complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Currently, the pathogenesis of T2DM-related sarcopenia remains unclear. The aim of this study was to investigate the molecular mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets for T2DM-related sarcopenia. In this study, a T2DM-related sarcopenia mouse model was established using db/db mice.

pmc-11531083.title: Experiences and Supportive Care Needs of Latinx Millennial Caregivers
pmc-11531083.creator: Catie Cleary, Galilea Dupree, Anna Welling, Janice F Hernandez, Heather Cuevas, Michael Thomas, Neil Peterson, Sharon D Horner, Megan Thomas Hebdon
pmc-11531083.description: Introduction:Latinx Millennial caregivers are an understudied minority group in the United States. Due to life stage and cultural values, these caregivers struggle to balance conflicting priorities with career, family, and caregiving. They also face systemic barriers and healthcare disparities.Methods:Participants (N = 29) were recruited locally and nationally. Qualitative data were collected using five focus groups and one individual interview.

pmc-12472345.title: Dual Enhancement of Optoelectronic and Mechanical Performance in Perovskite Solar Cells Enabled by Nanoplate-Structured FTO Interfaces
pmc-12472345.creator: Ruichen Tian, Aldrin D. Calderon, Quanrong Fang, Xiaoyu Liu
pmc-12472345.description: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) rarely report, on a single-device platform, concurrent gains in optoelectronic efficiency and buried-interface mechanical robustness—two prerequisites for flexible and roll-to-roll (R2R) integration. We engineered a nanoplate-structured fluorine-doped tin oxide (NP-FTO) front electrode that couples light management with three-dimensional interfacial anchoring, and we quantified both photovoltaic (PV) and nanomechanical metrics on the same device stack.

pmc-13355438.title: Renal vein thrombosis with inferior vena cava extension in PLA2R-positive membranous nephropathy: A radiological mimic of acute pyelonephritis
pmc-13355438.creator: Srikanth Nalla, Pravin Sudhakar Patil, Sumavally Maydari, Pawar Swathi
pmc-13355438.description: Renal vein thrombosis (RVT) is a recognized but often underdiagnosed complication of nephrotic syndrome, particularly in membranous nephropathy. We report the case of a 37-year-old male with PLA2R-positive membranous nephropathy who developed complete thrombosis of the left renal vein with extension into the inferior vena cava (IVC) over a length of approximately 5 cm.

uslaw-usc-t10-s8386.title: 10 U.S.C. § 8386 — Members of the Fleet Reserve and Fleet Marine Corps Reserve: release from active duty
uslaw-usc-t10-s8386.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s8386.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part II (Personnel); Chapter 845 (Recall To Active Duty). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Except as provided in subsection (b), the Secretary of the Navy may, at any time, release any member of the Fleet Reserve or the Fleet Marine Corps Reserve from active duty. (b) In time of war or national emergency declared.
